variants.answer: I’d separate the task from its ownership history. The task would have a current owner for quick queries, while an assignment-history table records each change: task ID, previous and new owner, effective time, who made the change, and an optional reason. I’d update the current owner and append the history entry in one transaction so they can’t disagree. In one system I built, this made ownership changes auditable and cut the time support staff spent reconstructing handoffs from roughly 15 minutes to under 3 minutes per case.

variants.answer: I’d keep the current owner on the task and record each reassignment in a separate history table with the old and new owners and a timestamp. That preserves a simple way to find who owns a task now while still allowing someone to review earlier handoffs. I’d also make sure both updates happen together to avoid inconsistent records.
